JAMBAVAN Guide

A simple field guide to task families, event playbooks, and accountable execution.

Simple execution · coaching institute edition

JAMBAVAN is a field guide, not a maze.

Use the task family that matches the size of the responsibility, then let the Event Planner turn a real institute program into a reusable execution playbook.

Task families

Choose the right level of work.

Every person can filter their feed by these categories. The category tells the team how much coordination and endurance the work needs.

S

Squirrel tasks

Small, focused contributions. One person, short horizon, clear finish line.

  • Best for quick follow-ups and simple actions
  • Usually one owner and no assistants
  • Example: confirm a batch-room booking
A

Angad tasks

One-person deliverables with weight. Bigger than a quick action, but still owned by one person.

  • Use for decks, reports, calls, and planned deliverables
  • One owner can add optional subtasks
  • Example: prepare the parent orientation deck
Su

Sugriv tasks

Coordinated team responsibilities. Multiple people contribute and everyone sees the shared progress.

  • Assign an owner plus multiple assistants
  • Add a separate responsibility note for each person
  • Only the owner marks the parent task complete
H

HANUMAN tasks

Long journeys and major responsibilities. Work that may run for months or a full year.

  • Keep progress updates and a growing subtask map
  • Use for strategic programs and institutional missions
  • Visible in the dedicated long-running workstream area
Event Planner workflow

Turn a program into a repeatable playbook.

Use this for parent orientations, admission drives, test series, faculty programs, and any event involving more than one department.

1Choose departmentsSelect every department involved, even when the event belongs to one department.
2Add roles and in-chargesRecord event head, coordinators, venue lead, or any other named responsibility.
3Add task rowsEach row gets a department, employee, category, and responsibility note.
4Save and reuseCreate the event and tasks now, or save the whole plan as a template for the next cycle.
